title: Horizons
credit_line: "Horizons" by Scott Buckley – released under CC-BY 4.0. www.scottbuckley.com.au
why: Melancholy piano and strings over a driving arpeggiated synth that propels forward: the clearest "progress over time" engine in the set.

title: Passage of Time
credit_line: "Passage of Time" by Scott Buckley – released under CC-BY 4.0. www.scottbuckley.com.au
why: Mysterious, solemn orchestral build toward a stately backend; written about time and old civilisations, matches the ENIAC → AI arc.

title: Signal to Noise
credit_line: "Signal to Noise" by Scott Buckley – released under CC-BY 4.0. www.scottbuckley.com.au
why: Solo cello and piano over warm synths and low strings: dark and warm like the film, intriguing rather than sad.

title: Machina
credit_line: "Machina" by Scott Buckley – released under CC-BY 4.0. www.scottbuckley.com.au
why: Glitchy electronic ambient in the style of 80s sci-fi scores; machine texture without being cold or playful.

title: Computations
credit_line: "Computations" by Scott Buckley – released under CC-BY 4.0. www.scottbuckley.com.au
why: Ambient electronics, strings and solo cello as a tonal soundscape; title and texture both fit a history of computing.

title: Tears in Rain
credit_line: "Tears in Rain" by Scott Buckley – released under CC-BY 4.0. www.scottbuckley.com.au
why: Subtle ambient synths and beats with simple piano, about losing memories to time: soft, warm, gently moving.

title: Half Mystery
credit_line: "Half Mystery" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com) · Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License · http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
why: Same synth+percussion family as Floating Cities; slow 72 bpm pulse "makes you think, but not too much".

title: Sincerely
credit_line: "Sincerely" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com) · Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License · http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
why: Floating Cities-adjacent synth bed; composer's note: "talk wistfully about the past, hopefully about the future".

title: Beauty Flow
credit_line: "Beauty Flow" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com) · Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License · http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
why: Old synth run through an arpeggiator: steady forward motion, same sound world as Floating Cities.

title: Unwritten Return
credit_line: "Unwritten Return" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com) · Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License · http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
why: Dreamy but edgy piano, synths and clavinet; mysterious without being dark.

title: Inexorable
credit_line: "Inexorable" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com) · Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License · http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
why: Processed piano over a ticking-clock figure; the most literal "time passing" texture (brash in places).

title: Atlantean Twilight
credit_line: "Atlantean Twilight" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com) · Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License · http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
why: Slow new-age piano where "time ticks away"; quiet and sparse, leaves room for narration.

title: Cylinder One
credit_line: "Cylinder One" by Chris Zabriskie · From the album Cylinders · Licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ · chriszabriskie.com
why: Minimal, repetitive synth cylinder pattern; feels like a machine slowly turning, very calm under voice.

title: Cylinder Five
credit_line: "Cylinder Five" by Chris Zabriskie · From the album Cylinders · Licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ · chriszabriskie.com
why: Most-used piece from Cylinders; hypnotic analogue pulse that reads as "documentary about technology".

title: Bigger Questions
credit_line: "Bigger Questions" by Lee Rosevere, licensed under CC BY 4.0 (creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
why: From Music for Podcasts – Serious, made to sit under narration; curious, thoughtful title and tone.

title: Making the Connections
credit_line: "Making the Connections" by Lee Rosevere, licensed under CC BY 4.0 (creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
why: Podcast-serious underscore built for voice; title echoes cables and connections (ENIAC patching).

title: Systematic
credit_line: "Systematic" by Lee Rosevere, licensed under CC BY 4.0 (creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
why: Podcast-serious underscore with a steadier, systematic feel; built to sit under narration.

title: Truth Be Told
credit_line: "Truth Be Told" by Maarten Schellekens, licensed under CC BY 4.0 (creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
why: Contemporary classical score cue (track is CC BY; most of his newer tracks are NC); cinematic, restrained.

title: Lullabies For The End Of The World #1
credit_line: Music: "Lullabies For The End Of The World #1" by HoliznaCC0 (CC0, no credit required)
why: CC0 fallback: soft soundtrack/chill-out bed, no attribution needed.

title: Prelude No. 1 in C major, BWV 846 (Open Well-Tempered Clavier)
artist: J.S. Bach, performed by Kimiko Ishizaka
credit_line: Music: Bach, Prelude in C major BWV 846, performed by Kimiko Ishizaka (Open Well-Tempered Clavier, CC0)
why: Endless cycling arpeggio feels algorithmic; a classical nod for a film about code. Also sold commercially (Navona), so a match is possible.
